claim: "All Tesla cars being produced now have full self-driving hardware."
why: Tesla later swapped that computer for a newer one, and in January 2025 Musk said cars on the next generation (HW3) will also need an upgrade for unsupervised driving.
q: "All Tesla Cars Being Produced Now Have Full Self-Driving Hardware" HW3 upgrade 2025

claim: "The person in the driver's seat is only there for legal reasons. He is not doing anything."
why: In a 2022 deposition, Tesla's Autopilot software director said the route was pre-mapped and the video did not show what the system could do on its own.
q: Tesla 2016 self-driving video staged deposition Elluswamy

claim: Sold an option called "Full Self-Driving Capability".
why: Years later the same product was renamed "Full Self-Driving (Supervised)", and California's DMV accused Tesla in 2022 of false advertising over the Autopilot and FSD names.
q: California DMV Tesla false advertising Autopilot Full Self-Driving

claim: Quarterly reports showing far fewer crashes per mile with Autopilot on.
why: Critics point out it compares mostly highway Autopilot miles with all US driving, which isn't like for like.
q: Tesla vehicle safety report Autopilot comparison criticism highway miles

claim: Owners will be able to add their car to a Tesla shared fleet and earn money while it drives others.
why: As far as we could find, no owner's car has joined a Tesla ride network that pays them.
q: Master Plan Part Deux shared fleet owners earn money

claim: Buying a car that isn't a Tesla is like buying a horse; your Tesla will be an appreciating asset worth well over $100,000 as a robotaxi.
why: Used Tesla prices have fallen, as with other cars, and we found no case of owners earning robotaxi income.
q: Musk Autonomy Day 2019 appreciating asset horse robotaxi

why: Both windows cracked on stage when a metal ball was thrown at them.

claim: Tri-motor Cybertruck with 500+ miles of range.
why: The top Cybertruck launched in 2023 with an estimated 320 miles.
q: Cybertruck 500 mile range promise 320 miles launch

claim: A "SpaceX option package" for the Roadster with rocket thrusters that let it hover.
why: The car it attaches to hasn't shipped.

claim: Optimus robots mingling with guests, serving drinks and chatting.
why: Reports afterwards said people were operating the robots remotely; that wasn't made clear on stage.
q: We Robot Optimus remotely operated teleoperated report

claim: Tesla Semi will be cheaper per mile than rail freight.
why: Only small fleets were running by 2026, and we couldn't find published data backing the rail comparison.
q: Musk Tesla Semi cheaper than rail 2017
